title: Any custom obj for Top stitch crashes Marvelous Designer
content:
Basically I have created a new top stitch, with the intention to import a simple custom obj mesh to be used for the stitching. The mesh is a simple chain link (comprised of 2 links). They are of a reasonable size and poly count (under 400 tris). Any attempt to import any object is met with a complete crash of marvelous designer. I've tested with a variety of simple objects made in maya and blender. ![06275e6926df4fee8cfadcf5dd32fa63](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/9af96d8f5ae649e3a6ecbe088c9b1311/images/06275e6926df4fee8cfadcf5dd32fa63MD_CrashBug.png)

My MD version is 2025.2.127

I've also tried importing these objects for topstitch on a fresh lighter file, still instant crash.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Issue resolved with our latest patch version 2025.2.143!

Comment 2: From our side, testing the tool do not crash the software. Please share with us the OBJ file used for the topstiches and the project file.Do so at our Contact Us page. We will take a look what is going on with your OBJhttps://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/9af96d8f5ae649e3a6ecbe088c9b1311
content_description: This page aims to address the issue of crashing in Marvelous Designer 2025.2.127 when importing custom OBJ meshes for a new top stitch, specifically a simple chain link design.

title: ELLi: Shaping a Daydream to a Digital Fantasy -  MDCC Vol3 2nd Place Award Winner
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/5f1d01f0486d47c6a3e697123df9c2a1/images/f252645328cc4bc592df1553808e8507WhatsApp%20Image%202025-09-21%20at%209.18.58%20AM.webp)_In this User Spotlight, we are thrilled to introduce Elli: 2nd place award winner in_[ _Marvelous Designer Creator's Contest 2025 Vol.3 "FANTASY ARCHIVES"._](https://connect.clo-set.com/contest/mdcc2025vol3)

## _ELLi discusses the story of her creation, and methods on how she created her entry for FANTASY ARCHIVES: the usage of Marvelous Designer to bring a rebellious Victorian queen to life._

![Award Thumbnail](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/marketplace/202509/878bf8922dce480e8086207c9c367452/1/thumbnail/WhatsApp%20Image%202025-09-21%20at%209.18.58%20AM.jpeg?w=2560)[Regal Rebel](https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/878bf8922dce480e8086207c9c367452)

* * *

**1\. Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

My name is Ella-Liencha and I live in South Africa. For years I searched for a way to express my creativity. I tried painting, drawing, and writing, but I always felt a pull toward something more - something that would allow my ideas to feel alive. In February 2025, at the age of 31, I discovered Marvelous Designer for the very first time. I had no background in 3D art or digital garment creation, yet the moment I opened the software, I was hooked!

My curiosity carried me through every step of the learning process. I was fascinated by how fabric could be shaped to appear structured or fluid, how folds and silhouettes could guide the viewer’s eye, and how each design could evoke an emotion or story. With every experiment, I fell deeper in love with the possibilities.

Participating in the Fantasy Archives competition was both an honor and a challenge. I felt I had everything to gain by simply trying. As a lifelong daydreamer, this theme felt like home, an invitation to bring my imagined worlds to life. Since I work a full-time job, most of this came together at night - hours of quiet crafting, stitching digital fabric together while my real world slept. It felt like threading my vision into the garment piece by piece: undoing, redoing, learning, and embracing the unpredictability of the process.

Through trial and error, I allowed myself to enjoy the process fully, to follow inspiration rather than control it. That freedom ultimately led me to the piece that placed, and I’m incredibly humbled and grateful for the recognition.

* * *

**2\. We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Creator’s contest 2025 Vol.3.  
What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

To be honest, my initial concept looked nothing like what “Regal Rebel” ultimately became. But the heart of the idea never changed: I wanted to create a queen-like figure who refuses to conform - someone powerful, elegant, and unapologetically rebellious.

My visual direction became a blend of Victorian influence and high fantasy - a meeting point between structure and softness, order and defiance. I experimented with how colors, fabrics, and textures could speak to one another: the richness of royalty intertwined with the unpredictability of rebellion.

![c303deda450e439a836af4f18f0721d7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/5f1d01f0486d47c6a3e697123df9c2a1/images/c303deda450e439a836af4f18f0721d7Untitled%20design%202.png)

Creating “Regal Rebel” felt very much like creating art itself. It was about pushing against boundaries, letting intuition lead, embracing mistakes, and trusting the process until the character revealed her true form.

Several symbolic choices shaped the final design.

**The external crinoline cage:**

Traditionally hidden beneath skirts, here it becomes visible and symbolic. It reflects the “cage” of the Victorian era, its expectations and constraints. By placing it on the outside, her rebellion becomes unmistakable.

**The shorts instead of a long Victorian skirt:**

Few things scream rebellion more loudly than wearing shorts in a period defined by restrictive dress! The ruffles and lace preserve the era’s dramatic volume without losing the bold statement.

Overall, the visual style aimed to capture a fantasy queen who embodies both grace and rebellion - someone who challenges tradition while still honoring the beauty of where she comes from.

![3d956cfa5d5f4e869d701567b2edab3d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/5f1d01f0486d47c6a3e697123df9c2a1/images/3d956cfa5d5f4e869d701567b2edab3dUntitled%20design%20%281%29%203.png)

* * *

**3\. Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer?  
Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

Oh wow! I have so much still to learn, and that honestly excites me more than anything. For Regal Rebel, my pipeline was simple but incredibly personal.

Marvelous Designer became my sketchbook, my mood board, and sometimes even my chaos playground. I drafted patterns, stitched them together, tore them apart again, reshaped them, and kept refining until the character started revealing who she wanted to be. It was a very intuitive process, less linear, more like sculpting with fabric and movement.

One of the biggest challenges was the armor elements. I wanted them to feel structured but not rigid, elegant but protective. Getting them to behave correctly in simulation meant playing and tweaking.

![f3fa4f7bf82a49fda904d744d8b10f50](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/5f1d01f0486d47c6a3e697123df9c2a1/images/f3fa4f7bf82a49fda904d744d8b10f502D-3D%20Marvelous%20Designer%203.JPG)

I also made heavy use of pressure simulation for the ruffled blouse and subtle gathers. Small changes in pressure and layering brought the softness and movement that helped balance the harsher armor.

The external crinoline cage was another adventure. Normally it would hide under a dress, but here I wanted it to stand proudly. Marvelous Designer’s curve tools and thickness settings let me shape it like a structural frame - symbolic, expressive, and unapologetically visible. Once the garments felt alive in Marvelous, I moved into Blender for the atmospheric side of the story.

![358ee9bf08ab4d28bcc0f03287309098](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/5f1d01f0486d47c6a3e697123df9c2a1/images/358ee9bf08ab4d28bcc0f032873090982D%203.JPG)

Creating the boot cuffs and lacing was surprisingly one of the most time-consuming steps. I rebuilt those pieces several times in Marvelous until the tension and direction of the straps felt believable. But once they finally worked, they grounded the entire silhouette.

![40799857c8784b2c8582183b588e393a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/5f1d01f0486d47c6a3e697123df9c2a1/images/40799857c8784b2c8582183b588e393a2D%20Close-Up%203.JPG)

In the end, Marvelous Designer gave me the structure and movement, and Blender let me wrap everything in emotion. Both tools together helped me bring Regal Rebel to life - a queen who stands in elegance, defiance, and power.

* * *

**4\. Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

If there’s one thing Marvelous Designer has taught me, it’s this: play. Be curious, be bold, be messy, be experimental. Don’t worry about always being “right” - worry about being _alive_ in your creativity.

I came into the 3D world with no background at all, and I realized very quickly that Marvelous Designer rewards those who explore. Every time I pushed a button I didn’t fully understand, every time a simulation exploded into chaos, every time I stitched the wrong line and everything collapsed, I learned something new. You are never too old, too new, or too inexperienced to follow your passion. But above all else: enjoy the process. Marvelous Designer is both a tool and a playground. Approach it with curiosity, and it will reward you with unexpected beauty.

If you’re stepping into 3D for the first time - welcome. It’s never too late, and your voice, your vision, and your story absolutely belong here. I am in awe every time I see the creators on Connect - their visions, their stories, the worlds they bring to life. They inspire me constantly. Being part of this community feels like my heart could burst; it’s one of my greatest motivators and one of the biggest joys of this journey.

* * *

title: Is it possible to "glue" sections of pattern pieces together in Marvelous Designer?
content:
I need to create a fabric object in which areas of pieces of fabric are glued together, not sewn. Only part not all of the pairs of pieces are glued so I can't just cheat it with a single piece. If I just sew the boundary of the glued area then the inner areas aren't flush. I can't find anything online about this. Thanks

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: The Tack tool lets you "glue" two areas or points of different patterns together. Is that what you're looking for?
Reply 1: I've used the Tack tool before. I know there's regular point tacks, and line tacks... what I really need is like an "area tack" where you would paint select an area of polygons on each mesh which would then get stuck together, flush. Maybe a feature to request!
content_description: This web page aims to provide guidance and techniques for creating fabric objects using selective gluing methods to achieve a flush finish without sewing the entire piece.

title: Meet Anny Han: 2nd Place Winner of MDCC Vol.2!
content:
## _Meet Anny Han, a 3D fashion and graphic designer with a deep background in pattern making and garment construction.  
By bridging traditional techniques with digital tools, she created a realistic, emotionally resonant digital fashion, resulting to her award of 2nd Place in the _[_Marvelous Designer Creator's Contest Vol.2 " TOKYO CONTINUUM - 東京進化系 -"!_](https://connect.clo-set.com/contest/mdcc2025vol2)

* * *

![44e8b1862dea4ef4aeaac508b9fdf6ef](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/6db6acc9f1144f13a8bd11a6a0645519/images/44e8b1862dea4ef4aeaac508b9fdf6ef4.webp)[花と爆 (Hana to Baku)](https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/57c70236280a403997e3eef3deae4f99)

* * *

### **1\. Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

**Anny Han:** Hello, my name is Anny Han, and I am a 3D fashion and graphic designer.

I currently work in fashion product development, using CLO and Marvelous Designer to create realistic digital garments based on my background in pattern making and construction. I first started learning 3D to improve communication and speed within the development process, and it soon became an essential tool for expressing my own creative world.

I joined this contest to explore new styles and push myself beyond my usual workflow as a creator. Through this experience, I gained clearer direction in building my own aesthetic and artistic identity in 3D.

![5d97640ccfb84ee29598e03aeb2b69b9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/6db6acc9f1144f13a8bd11a6a0645519/images/5d97640ccfb84ee29598e03aeb2b69b9image.png)

* * *

### **2\. We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Creator’s contest 2025 Vol.3. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

**Anny Han:** For this project, I aimed to express the **dual identity** experienced by many young people living in modern cities.

The “Bomb (ボム)” on the back and the “Flower (花)” in the hand symbolize the contrast between destruction and beauty, resistance and acceptance—visualizing the conflicting emotions that coexist within today’s youth.

The overall art direction focused on the **intersection of tradition and modernity**. Inspired by traditional Japanese silhouettes and textiles, I reinterpreted these heritage elements through a contemporary and functional lens. I incorporated delicate stitchwork inspired by **Sashiko** , a traditional Japanese embroidery technique, to bring a rhythmic and meditative craftsmanship to the garment.

To balance this with a modern sensibility, I added technical pockets and a bold graphic bag to enhance practicality, creating a bridge between the past and the future.

The flower motif, blooming like an explosion, serves as the centerpiece of the look—turning the garment into a powerful form of visual storytelling.

![3D 花と爆 \(Hana to Baku\) Model](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/marketplace/202505/57c70236280a403997e3eef3deae4f99/thumbnail/2.png?resize=1&f=webp&w=1680&fit=scale-down)

* * *

### **3\. Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

![a937a8de69ef46f0b15868e10901916c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/6db6acc9f1144f13a8bd11a6a0645519/images/a937a8de69ef46f0b15868e10901916cimage.png)

**Anny Han:** I began by creating the garment 2D pattern in a CLO program. Thanks to my background in pattern making, building the base structure was not difficult, but I focused on ensuring the garment made structural sense in real life.

In Marvelous Designer, I refined the silhouette by adjusting ease, natural wrinkles, and three-dimensional shape. After assembling the garment, I conducted quick color tests directly inside MD to explore different palettes. Separating parts into UV areas allowed me to manage materials and colors more efficiently throughout the process.

* * *

### **4\. Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

**Anny Han:** One thing I’ve learned is that continuously studying other creators’ work is essential. Seeing different approaches and styles always pushes me to grow, and I still feel that I have a lot to learn.

Rather than relying only on my own habits, I try to broaden my perspective by observing how others use Marvelous Designer and how they express details.

These days, I believe combining Marvelous Designer with AI tools can elevate the quality of a project even further—whether for ideation, reference gathering, or enhancing the final presentation.

Staying open to new tools and new ways of working is, for me, the most important tip.

* * *

content_description: Discover the innovative fusion of traditional craftsmanship and modern technology in the work of Anny Han, a talented 3D fashion and graphic designer renowned for her award-winning digital garments.
